claim.pdf_says: 'ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1' with EXCEPTION underlined; 'NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2' with NOT and EXCEPTION underlined (ON is NOT underlined in either row).
claim.why_it_matters: The whole exception block is transcribed with zero underline markup even though the surrounding figure (ACCEPT, FROM, LINE, COLUMN, END-ACCEPT) uses \underline throughout, so the required-word/optional-word distinction is silently lost exactly where it matters: EXCEPTION and NOT are required, ON is optional. A reader cannot tell that 'NOT EXCEPTION' is legal and that 'EXCEPTION' cannot be omitted.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED against both sources at 300 dpi. PDF (spec_p607.png, ACCEPT Format 3 (screen), printed page 577): I cropped the exception block and enlarged it 2x-4x. Row 1 reads 'ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1' -- there is no rule beneath 'ON'; a single continuous rule runs beneath EXCEPTION only, starting under the 'E' and ending under the final 'N'. Row 2 reads 'NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2' -- a short rule runs beneath 'NOT' and terminates before 'ON', there is a clear unruled gap under 'ON', then a second rule runs beneath 'EXCEPTION'. imperative-statement-1/-2 are unruled. So the claim's reading of the printed glyphs is exactly correct. MARKDOWN (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25265, identical to the workunit page-607.md line 10) is verbatim: $$\left[\begin{array}{l} \text{ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1} \\ \text{NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2} \end{array}\right]$$ -- zero \underline anywhere in the block, and no compensating figure note (grep of the page-607 region finds none; the '⎡| ... |⎤' ASCII figures with 'Required words (underlined in the printed figure)' notes at lines 25695/25732/25738 belong to CALL Format 2, a different statement). REFUTATION ATTEMPTS, ALL FAILED: (a) the markup is not present reflowed or on an adjacent line -- the whole figure is one $$...$$ line; (b) this is not formatting/line-wrap furniture -- per ISO 5.2.6, underlining in a general format is the sole notation distinguishing REQUIRED words from OPTIONAL words, so dropping it drops derivable syntax, not typography; (c) the claim misquotes neither source -- both quotes match byte-for-byte / glyph-for-glyph; (d) meaning does change -- as transcribed, a reader or grammar author cannot tell that 'ACCEPT scr EXCEPTION imp-1' and 'ACCEPT scr NOT EXCEPTION imp-2' are legal (ON omissible) while 'EXCEPTION' and 'NOT' are not omissible. The transcription's own convention is proven live and selectively applied in the immediately adjacent lines -- line 25264 writes \underline{\text{LINE}} while leaving \text{AT} and \text{NUMBER} plain, exactly matching the PDF -- which rules out any 'this transcription simply never marks underlines' defence. The claim's premise sentence is the only inaccurate part: the surrounding figure does NOT use \underline 'throughout'. In the same $$ block the PDF underlines BOTH alternatives of the COLUMN/COL brace (verified in colzoom.png: separate rules under 'COLUMN' and under 'COL'), but the markdown writes \underline{\text{COLUMN}} and plain \text{COL} -- a sibling underline loss that makes COL look like an optional word rather than a required alternative. That overstatement does not weaken the finding; it is a second instance of it.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with a broadened scope. In the ACCEPT Format 3 (screen) general format on page 607, the markdown loses THREE pieces of figure notation, not one. (1) The exception block is transcribed as plain \text{} with no underline markup: the PDF underlines EXCEPTION in row 1, and underlines NOT and EXCEPTION (but not ON) in row 2, so the transcription silently erases that ON is an optional word while EXCEPTION and NOT are required -- 'ACCEPT scr EXCEPTION imp-1' / 'NOT EXCEPTION imp-2' are legal and the transcription cannot show it. (2) The same figure drops the underline on COL: the PDF underlines both COLUMN and COL as required alternatives of the brace, the markdown writes \underline{\text{COLUMN}} but plain \text{COL}, wrongly demoting COL to an optional word. (3) More severely, the exception block's delimiters are mis-transcribed: the PDF prints BRACKETS WITH CHOICE INDICATORS -- verified in exc_left.png as '[' immediately followed by a full-height vertical bar, and in exc_right.png as a full-height vertical bar immediately followed by ']' (the '⎡| ... |⎤' form) -- which per ISO 5.2.6.4 means zero or more of the enclosed alternatives, each at most once, in any order, i.e. ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION may BOTH appear in one ACCEPT, in either order. The markdown renders it as a plain \left[ ... \right] around a two-row stack, which reads as ordinary zero-or-one selection and thus wrongly forbids specifying both phrases. Note the same transcription already documents the correct '⎡| ... |⎤' semantics for the identical CALL Format 2 block (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25738), so page 607 is inconsistent with the file's own established treatment. Fix: mark \underline on EXCEPTION (row 1), NOT and EXCEPTION (row 2), and COL; and render the exception block with choice indicators plus a figure note matching the CALL Format 2 note.
